about.intro: Ori Studio aims to be the ultimate workspace for origami design and analysis. It leans heavily on ports of existing origami tools created by the community — the Edit workspace, for instance, is a port of Oriedita to Rust, focused on usability and performance. If you have any suggestions, feel free to <2>open an issue on GitHub</2>.
about.subtitle: A modern shared workspace for designing, editing, and folding origami crease patterns.
about.title: About Ori Studio

boxPleatingStudio.detail: The box-pleated authoring method is a Rust and WebAssembly port of Mu-Tsun Tsai's Box Pleating Studio.
boxPleatingStudio.title: Mu-Tsun Tsai and Box Pleating Studio

explori.detail: The Search 22.5° design method sends your tree to ExplOri, a searchable archive of 22.5° crease patterns, and shows the closest matches it returns.
explori.title: Brandon Wong and ExplOri 22.5

oriedita.detail: The crease-pattern editor is a Rust and WebAssembly port of the Oriedita editor (itself a fork of Orihime), including its foldability diagnostics, repairs, and file formats.
oriedita.title: Oriedita

origamiSimulator.detail: The Simulate workspace folds bases into an interactive 3D model using a TypeScript port of Amanda Ghassaei's Origami Simulator.
origamiSimulator.title: Amanda Ghassaei and Origami Simulator

treemaker.detail: TreeMaker's original model code and behavior are the canonical reference for this Rust, WebAssembly, and desktop port.
treemaker.title: Robert J. Lang and TreeMaker 5.0.1

orieditaImport.intro: In Oriedita, open Preferences and choose Export to write a .oriconfig file.
orieditaImport.noCustomizations: This export has no edited hotkeys, so there is nothing to carry over. To use Oriedita's layout, turn on Oriedita defaults in Settings ▸ Shortcuts.

reason.altGraph: Uses AltGr, which Ori Studio cannot match.
reason.ambiguousEmpty: Left blank in Oriedita. Oriedita writes the same blank when a hotkey is reset to its default, so this one is left alone.
reason.ctrlMeta: Holds Control and Command together, which Ori Studio treats as one modifier.
reason.keyLocation: Uses a numeric keypad key, which a browser cannot tell apart from the main keyboard.
reason.menuAccelerator: Menu shortcuts cannot use this key.
reason.modifierOnly: Records only modifier keys, with nothing to press with them.
reason.noKeystroke: No key was recorded for this hotkey.
reason.notBindable: This action cannot take an imported shortcut.
reason.released: Fires when the key is let go, which Ori Studio does not do.
reason.reserved: The browser keeps this shortcut for itself.
reason.shadowedTakes: Would take this key away from {{action}}.
reason.shadowedWithinImport: Another hotkey in this import already wants this key.
reason.shiftNonLetter: Shift with a number or punctuation key means a different character in a browser, so this shortcut could never fire.
reason.typedCharacter: Records a typed character rather than a key, so the key to bind depends on the keyboard layout.
reason.unknownKey: Uses a key Ori Studio does not know.
reason.unmappedAction: Ori Studio has no matching action.
reason.unreadable: This hotkey could not be read.
